Theme

Civic life: news, government & the law

domestic adjective

of one’s own country, not foreign

also home (as against foreign), internal, home-grown, domestic politics, civil war, at home and abroad, on the home front

classical

Cic. Off. 2.26: externa libentius in tālī rē quam domestica recordor
Caes. BG 2.10.4: domesticae cōpiae reī frūmentāriae (Lewis & Short)

domesticus, domestica, domesticum

declension

of one’s own country, native, internal (opposed to foreign)

Against externus or peregrīnus (see foreign): one’s own people’s customs, examples, resources, enemies; bellum domesticum, civil war (Lewis & Short). Its first sense is “of the household” (see domestic, of the home and family).

Other words

  • intestīnus, intestīna, intestīnum — internal, within the state (of war, strife, evils)

    declension · also used · classical · Cic. Cat. 2.28: bellum intestīnum ac domesticum

    “Inward, internal”, of trouble inside the state: bellum intestīnum, discordia intestīna (Lewis & Short). As a noun, intestīna are the guts.

Examples

  • Externa libentius in tālī rē quam domestica recordor.

    In a matter like this I prefer to recall foreign examples rather than our own.Cic. Off. 2.26

  • bellum intestīnum ac domesticum post hominum memoriam crūdēlissimum et maximum

    the cruellest and greatest civil war within the memory of manCic. Cat. 2.28

  • domī et mīlitiae

    on the home front and on the war front, in peace and warLewis & Short s.v. domus: domī mīlitiaeque, in war and peace; Traupman 329

See also domestic, foreign, national, international.
